dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef004
dependency_coverage.meaning: Projects the third field of a run, a vector b : Fin m -> Real.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef005
dependency_coverage.meaning: Projects the fourth field of a run, the real scalar b_K.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef006

dependency_coverage.meaning: Projects the eighteenth field of a run, the computed real output yHat.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef009
dependency_coverage.meaning: The inductive type of floating-point formats constructed by D011.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef010
dependency_coverage.meaning: Constructs a run from a format F; vectors a and b; scalars b_K and c; representability proofs for all inputs; b_K != 0; safe-range proofs for every exact product a_i b_i; an m+1-leaf summation tree and a permutation; validity of rounded evaluation of the permuted vector whose entries are c and -round(a_i b_i); a numerator N equal to that rounded evaluation; an accumulation relation for N with exact correction -sum_i a_i b_i and absolute-size bound sum_i |a_i b_i|; and an output yHat satisfying yHat = N when b_K = 1 and yHat = round(N/b_K), with N/b_K safe, when b_K != 1.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Specifies all admissibility and computation assumptions hidden in the universally quantified run.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef011
dependency_coverage.meaning: Constructs a floating-point format with radix beta, precision p, exponent limits, a finite representable set, safe-range and rounding operations, and unit roundoff u. It requires beta >= 2, p > 0, ordered exponent limits, a one-way normalized representation characterization, 0 <= u <= 1/2, u(2 beta^(p-1)) = 1, representability of 0 and 1 and closure under negation, representable rounded safe values, nearest-representable rounding, the relative model |round(x)-x| <= u|round(x)| on the safe range, nonnegativity preservation, a stated rounded-square-root bound, and exact rounding of representable values.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Constrains the format underlying every run and, in particular, makes the bound parameter u nonnegative and at most 1/2.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef012
dependency_coverage.meaning: Projects the representable : Real -> Prop field of a format.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Used indirectly to require representable inputs, leaves, intermediate computed values, and outputs in the bundled run.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef013
dependency_coverage.meaning: Projects the round : Real -> Real field of a format.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Defines rounded products, rounded tree additions, and the division result used to form yHat.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef014
dependency_coverage.meaning: Projects the safeRange : Real -> Prop field of a format.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Restricts products, tree additions, and nontrivial division in admissible runs.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef015
dependency_coverage.meaning: An inductively generated accumulation relation A_F(k,p,e,s,z). Its base and step rules are D020 and D021; it tracks a pivot p, an accumulated exact correction e, an absolute-size bound s, and a final computed value z over k terms.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: A run must contain A_F(m+1,c,-sum_i a_i b_i,sum_i |a_i b_i|,N), which supplies the accumulated-error structure behind the existential perturbations.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef018

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef019

dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Ensures that every rounded addition used to compute the numerator satisfies the format assumptions.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef020

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef021
dependency_coverage.meaning: Step rule for the accumulation relation. A sibling block of positive count l with exact value e_s, bound s_s >= |e_s|, representable computed value z_s, and |z_s-e_s| <= l u s_s may be added safely to pivot p; if the remainder satisfies A_F(k,round(p+z_s),e_o,s_o,z), then A_F(k+l,p,e_s+e_o,s_s+s_o,z).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Propagates local rounded-block errors into the aggregate relation used for the numerator.

binders: m is universally quantified over the natural numbers; m = 0 is allowed.

run is universally quantified over LocalDef002 m. It bundles a floating-point format F, vectors a,b : Fin m -> R, scalars b_K and c, a computed numerator N, an output yHat, an m+1-leaf summation tree T, a permutation pi of Fin(m+1), and validity proofs.
The first conclusion existentially quantifies a real scalar theta_0 and a function theta : Fin m -> R.
Under b_K = 1, the second conclusion existentially quantifies another real scalar theta_0 and function theta : Fin m -> R; these witnesses need not equal those from the first conclusion.
hypotheses: The format F has radix beta >= 2, precision p > 0, ordered integer exponent limits, a finite representable set, a safe-range predicate, a rounding operation, and unit roundoff u satisfying 0 <= u <= 1/2 and u(2 beta^(p-1)) = 1.

Every representable x is either zero or has the form x = q beta^(e-(p-1)), where q and e are integers, |q| < beta^p, and the exponent lies between the format limits. This is only a necessary characterization, not an encoded converse.

The format represents 0 and 1, is closed under negation, rounds safe values to representable values, chooses a nearest representable value, satisfies |round(x)-x| <= u|round(x)| on its safe range, preserves nonnegativity there, satisfies the stated rounded-square-root bound, and fixes representable values exactly.
For every i : Fin m, a_i and b_i are representable; b_K and c are representable; b_K != 0; and each exact product a_i b_i is in the safe range.

The run stores an m+1-leaf binary tree T and a permutation pi. For the vector v with v_0 = c and v_(i+1) = -round(a_i b_i), every leaf of v composed with pi is representable and every tree addition is in the safe range.
The stored numerator N equals the rounded tree evaluation of v composed with pi.
The run includes the accumulation relation A_F(m+1,c,-sum_i a_i b_i,sum_i |a_i b_i|,N).
The output satisfies b_K = 1 -> yHat = N; if b_K != 1, then N/b_K is in the safe range and yHat = round(N/b_K).
The sharper second conclusion has the additional antecedent b_K = 1.
conclusions: There exist theta_0 in R and theta : Fin m -> R such that |theta_0| <= (m+1)u, every |theta_i| <= (m+1)u, and b_K yHat (1+theta_0) = c - sum_{i in Fin m} a_i b_i (1+theta_i).
If b_K = 1, there exist potentially different theta_0 in R and theta : Fin m -> R such that |theta_0| <= m u, every |theta_i| <= m u, and yHat (1+theta_0) = c - sum_{i in Fin m} a_i b_i (1+theta_i).
mathematical_definitions: Write u for the unit roundoff of the run's format, a_i = a(i), and b_i = b(i). Natural counts m and m+1 are cast to real numbers when multiplied by u.
Fin m represents the indices 0,...,m-1. Every displayed sum is over all these indices and is zero when m = 0.
The exact numerator represented in the final identities is S = c - sum_i a_i b_i.

The computed product at index i is p_i = round(a_i b_i). Define v_0 = c and v_(i+1) = -p_i. The stored numerator N is obtained by permuting the entries of v by pi and recursively summing them according to T, rounding once at each internal tree node.
The tree-validity predicate requires representable leaves and safe-range unrounded additions of the two already computed child results at every internal node.

The accumulation relation A_F has base A_F(1,p,0,0,p) for representable p. Its step combines a sibling block of count l > 0, exact value e_s, nonnegative bound s_s with |e_s| <= s_s, and representable computed value z_s satisfying |z_s-e_s| <= l u s_s. If p+z_s is safe and A_F(k,round(p+z_s),e_o,s_o,z) holds, then A_F(k+l,p,e_s+e_o,s_s+s_o,z) holds.

The first identity is a componentwise relative backward-error representation for c and the exact products a_i b_i, with a separate multiplicative perturbation on b_K yHat. The second removes b_K because its antecedent fixes b_K exactly to 1.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every natural dimension m and every admissible bundled floating-point run of that dimension, the computed output admits a backward-error representation: one can perturb the output-side factor and every exact product a_i b_i by relative factors 1+theta, with all perturbations bounded in absolute value by (m+1)u, so that the resulting equality with c holds exactly. Moreover, when b_K is exactly 1, possibly different perturbations exist with the sharper bound m u and the exact equality uses yHat directly.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The theorem ranges only over values of the highly constrained run type; it does not assert that such a run exists for every m, format, or raw input data.
The conditional sharper conclusion is logically vacuous whenever b_K != 1.
The dimension m may be zero. Then Fin m is empty, all componentwise bounds are vacuous, and all sums are empty. In the b_K = 1 branch the scalar bound is |theta_0| <= 0.
The witnesses in the two conjuncts are independent, and no uniqueness, sign, or correspondence with particular local rounding errors is asserted.
No smallness assumption such as (m+1)u < 1 is encoded. Consequently the factors 1+theta_0 and 1+theta_i are not asserted to be nonzero or positive.
The bounds are the linear quantities (m+1)u and m u, not gamma factors with denominators.
The final identities use exact products a_i b_i and an exact finite sum; the rounded products, permutation, and rounded tree evaluation occur only in the bundled computation assumptions.
The conclusion is a backward-error identity, not a direct forward-error or relative-error bound between yHat and the exact quotient (c-sum_i a_i b_i)/b_K.
The safe-range predicate is abstract and has no explicit numerical interval characterization in the proposition.
The format representation axiom says that representable values have a normalized form, but does not state that every value of that form is representable.
All norms in the conclusion are scalar real absolute values; no vector or matrix norm is encoded.
